exposure: delivery period (2020-2022, associated with COVID-19 pandemic)
cohort: The study included 1,118,842 in-hospital deliveries that occurred in Ecuador between 2015 and 2022.
finding: Cesarean section rates in Ecuador (41.3%) exceed recommended levels, and sociodemographic factors such as maternal age, ethnicity, and healthcare facility type are significantly associated with the probability of c-section, with an increase in emergency c-sections observed during the 2020-2022 COVID-19 pandemic period.
mod_finding: The study found that sociodemographic factors influenced the probability of both overall c-sections and specific types (elective or emergency c-section), with some factors showing differential associations with elective versus emergency procedures.
